summary: James Matthew Baskind is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied under doctoral supervisor Stanley Weinstein at Yale University, where he earned a PhD (attested 2006).

James McHugh specializes in Indology and religious studies. He studied at Cambridge, Oxford (under Benson, Gombrich, Sanderson, Smith, and Teichman), and Harvard (PhD under McCrea, Monius, and Patil), holding posts at Cornell and the University of Southern California.

James Miller (born 1968) is a scholar of Sinology and religious studies. He earned an MA from Cambridge (by 1997) and a PhD from Boston University (by 2000), later serving as Professor at Queen's University Belfast (attested 2014).
James Morison is an Indologist who studied under Georg Bühler. He served as Librarian at the Indian Institute, University of Oxford (attested 1917–1920).

James Murdoch (1856–1921) was a scholar of Japanology and history/archaeology. He studied at Aberdeen (~1874–1879) and under Theodor Benfey (~1879–1880), later holding posts at the University of Tokyo (~1889–1893), Kanazawa (~1900–1901), and Kagoshima (~1901–1908).

James Prinsep (1799–1840) was an Indologist and historian/archaeologist. He served at the Benares Mint (~1820–1830) and Kolkata Mint (1819, 1830–1838), led The Asiatic Society (1832–1838), founded the Journal of the Asiatic Society of Bengal, and founded Corpus Inscriptionum Indicarum.

James Robert Ballantyne (1813–1864) worked in Indology, philosophy, and linguistics. Educated at Edinburgh (~1828–1832) under James Michael and Francis Johnson, he served as master at the Scottish Naval and Military Academy (1832–1845), Principal of Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (1845–1861), and India Office librarian.

James Robson (born 1965) specializes in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. Educated at UC Santa Barbara (~1983–1987) and Stanford (PhD ~1996–2002), he taught at Williams College, Michigan (2004–2008), and Harvard, becoming Harvard-Yenching Institute director in 2024.

James Smith Reid (1846–1926) was an historian and archaeologist. Educated at Cambridge (~1865–1869), he held positions at Christ's College (1869–1880), Pembroke College (1873–1885), and Gonville and Caius College (1878–1926).

James Sutherland Cotton (1847–1918) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. Educated at Trinity College, Oxford (1867–1870), he held posts at Queens' College, Cambridge (1871–1874) and Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (1871–1874).

James Tod (1782–1835) was an Indologist and historian who studied at the Royal Military Academy, Woolwich (~1797–1798) and under Gyanchandra (~1812–1823). He served with the East India Company (~1798–1822) and as Librarian of the Royal Asiatic Society (~1823–1835).

James W. Benson is a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He held faculty posts at Harvard University (attested 1999), the University of Oxford (attested 1999), and Wolfson College, Oxford (attested 2001).

James W. Heisig (born 1944) works in philosophy, religious studies, and Japanology. Educated at Divine Word College, Loyola, Notre Dame, and Cambridge (PhD ~1969–1973), he held posts at Divine Word College and Nanzan University, including the Nanzan Institute (~1978–2005).
James Ward (1843–1925) was a philosopher. He studied at Fitzwilliam College and Trinity College, Cambridge (~1872–1875), and held an academic post at the University of Cambridge from ~1897 to 1925.
James Whitehill is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy. He founded the Columbia Zen Center and served as Professor of Religion at Stephens College (attested 2000).

James Wilson Bright (1852–1926) was a linguist who studied at Lafayette College (~1871–1875) and earned his PhD from Johns Hopkins (~1879–1882). He taught at Cornell (~1885) and held the Caroline Donovan Chair of English at Johns Hopkins (1905–1925).

Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso (1846–1912) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Tibetology. He studied under teachers including Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo (~1860–1892), Patrul Rinpoche (~1860–1887), and Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye (~1860–1899).

Jamgon Kongtrul Lodro Chokyi Senge (1954–1992) was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under the 16th Karmapa Rangjung Rigpe Dorje, Kalu Rinpoche (1973), Khenchen Thrangu Rinpoche, and Nyoshul Khenpo Rinpoche.

Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye (1813–1899) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He studied under numerous teachers, notably Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo (~1840–1892), Tekchok Dorje (~1833–1868), Tai Situ Pema Nyinje Wangpo (~1833–1853), and Chokgyur Dechen Lingpa (~1853–1870).

Jamie Hubbard is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied at Komazawa University and under Minoru Kiyota at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (PhD), later holding professorships at Smith College (attested 2016, 2026).
